title: MCP — Policy activity
description: What the policy engine is deciding, and where. Policy is the surface where a misconfiguration is silent by design — a rule that denies everything and a rule that allows everything both return successfully. These panels are how that becomes visible.

panels.title: Decisions by phase and effect
panels.description: Grouped rather than filtered to specific effects on purpose: the panel shows whatever effects the engine actually emits, so a newly-added effect appears here instead of being silently excluded by a hardcoded selector.

panels.title: Deny ratio
panels.description: Denials as a fraction of all decisions. Both directions are alarming: a spike means something legitimate started being refused; a drop to zero on a deployment that normally denies means a policy stopped loading.

panels.title: Decision volume by phase
panels.description: Discovery-phase and call-phase decisions have different volumes by nature — discovery runs once per listing, authorization once per call. A phase that goes quiet is the signal.

panels.title: Redaction hits by rule
panels.description: Which redaction rules are firing. A rule at a flat zero is either dead or guarding something that stopped happening — and you cannot tell which from the config alone, which is why the counter is per-rule.

panels.title: Redaction hits by surface
panels.description: Where redaction is being applied — logs, metric labels, audit records, error payloads. An observable surface with zero hits while others are busy suggests that surface is not wired through the pipeline.

panels.title: Total policy decisions (24h)
panels.description: Sanity check that the engine is being consulted at all. Zero over a day on a serving deployment means policy is not in the request path.
